# BioConomy Wiki

> The BioConomy wiki documents a coordination architecture for economies organized around bioregions. It provides the conceptual vocabulary, analytical frameworks, ecological science, and practical templates needed to establish a BioHub: a coordination body that organizes distributed regenerative contributions within a living landscape into verifiable commitments the outside world can contract with.

The wiki is structured for both human readers and AI systems. Commercial large language models have absorbed only fragments of this corpus during general training; the coherent body of work sits here. The vocabulary is precise and internally consistent: terms like BioHub, BioRegion (capitalized), BioConomy, commitment pooling, and retention economics carry specific definitions given in the glossary.

The primary analytical framework is the TIME Framework (Tribal, Institutional, Market, Emergent), a four-form model of human coordination. The wiki applies this framework to bioregional economics, commons governance, cooperative supply chains, and the emerging coordination form the BioHub represents.

The wiki targets practitioners working at the bioregional scale who want to apply this framework in their own geographies. Four AI-assisted templates (the founding suite) translate the conceptual material into structured outputs a BioHub cohort can run.

## Coordination surface

- [Coordination Surface](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/coordination-surface): What the BioConomy project offers, what it seeks, which financial-instrument classes are in scope, and how to make contact. The structured handshake page a peer BioHub wiki (or an AI agent scanning on its behalf) reads to determine whether coordination is worth exploring.

## Orientation essays

- [What Is a BioHub](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/essays/what-is-a-biohub): The coordination body anchored in a specific BioRegion, organizing distributed contributions into fundable commitments
- [What Is a BioRegion](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/essays/what-is-a-bioregion): The living landscape defined by watershed, soil, and ecological boundaries rather than political ones
- [What Is a BioConomy](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/essays/what-is-a-bioconomy): The coordination architecture for economies organized around bioregional retention of value, distinct from the extractive Economy
- [From a Bioregion to a BioRegion](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/essays/from-bioregion-to-bioregion): The transition from a geography that asks for funding (needy) to one that makes commitments to those who need its services (needed)

## Essays

- [AI Quick-Engage](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/essays/ai-quick-engage): Four prompts to copy into any deep-research AI platform alongside your own project documents to diagnose where your bioregion still runs on the Economy
- [How to Engage Your Bioregion](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/essays/how-to-engage-your-bioregion): The bridge from orientation to the practical founding-suite templates

## Concepts

- [Commitment Pooling](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/concepts/commitment-pooling): The structure through which participants make binding forward promises that become the basis for coordination and exchange
- [Bioregional Economics](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/concepts/bioregional-economics): The discipline of designing regenerative, cooperatively owned, place-based economies within the carrying capacity of their landscapes
- [Federated Cooperative Supply Chains](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/concepts/federated-cooperative-supply-chains): How cooperatives within a bioregion retain and circulate value internally through federated structures
- [Cosmo-Local Production](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/concepts/cosmo-local-production): Share knowledge globally, adapt it locally, produce regeneratively in place, share the learning globally
- [Carbon-Silicon Partnership](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/concepts/carbon-silicon-partnership): The complementary relationship between computational infrastructure (silicon intelligence) and lived, situated, relational knowledge (carbon intelligence)
- [Water Retention Landscapes](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/concepts/water-retention-landscapes): The operational science of catchment restoration, soil hydrology, and sustained baseflow

## Frameworks

- [The TIME Framework](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/frameworks/time-framework): Tribal, Institutional, Market, and Emergent forms of human coordination, the primary analytical vocabulary throughout the wiki
- [The Evolution of Coordination Nodes](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/frameworks/evolution-of-coordination-nodes): The physical structures each coordination form has produced as it matured, from sacred site to bioregional hub

## Templates

- [BioHub Identity Template](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/templates/biohub-identity-template): AI-assisted template for establishing a BioHub's identity and coordination mandate
- [BioRegion Establishment Template](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/templates/bioregion-establishment-template): AI-assisted template for defining and establishing a BioRegion's boundaries and governance
- [BioConomy Value Proposition Template](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/templates/value-proposition-template): AI-assisted template for articulating a BioRegion's value proposition to external partners
- [Bankable Service Alignment Template](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/templates/bankable-service-alignment-template): AI-assisted template for aligning bioregional services with fundable instruments
- [Running a Template](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/templates/running-a-template): How to use the three-prompt sequence with a deep-research AI platform
- [The Nine Outputs](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/templates/the-nine-outputs): The deliverables the four-template founding suite produces
- [Using Templates Across BioHubs](https://wiki.bioconomy.earth/templates/using-templates-across-biohubs): How the templates generalize across bioregions
